Fix a flag for one end user (on, off or a variant) in production, or in test with --env test,
whatever its rules and rollout say. 'clear' lets the flag decide for them again.

A flag that is off in an environment stays off there for everyone, overrides included.

With -q it prints the flag's id, since an override has none of its own. With --json it prints the
override, or the flag after 'clear'.

Usage:
  voidhash flag override [flag] [person] [setting] [flags]

Arguments:
  flag     The flag's key or id
  person   The end user: an email, a distinct id or a person id (person_…); prefix email:,
           distinct_id:, person_id: or external_id: to say which
  setting  on, off, a variant (its value, label or id), or clear

Flags:
      --env <production|test>  The environment: production, or test, which apps using a test key
                               read; test follows production until something is changed in it
  -h, --help                   Show help for this command
      --json                   Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --note <note>            Why, such as QA
      --project <project>      Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default:
                               this directory's project, then your default project)
  -q, --quiet                  Print only ids, one per line

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash flag override new-checkout alice@example.com on
  voidhash flag override button-color device-1234 blue --env test --note QA
  voidhash flag override new-checkout alice@example.com clear
